solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: House right next to moors proved inadequate

indicators.note: next to says the house and right pieces sit right after the moors piece

parts.note: fells are high open moorland hills in northern England

explanation.surface: A building beside the moors turned out not to be good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: FELLS are the moorland hills of northern England; HO and RT are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to come up short of a target is to prove inadequate, past tense to match.

clue.text: Thrash learner, overwhelmed by disappointing test result

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the learner is engulfed by the test result word

parts.note: a fail is a disappointing outcome in a test
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Beat the learner driver who flunked their test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' puts L inside FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to thrash about is to wave limbs wildly, flapping and beating.

clue.text: Eagle with endless pluck going over lake

indicators.note: going over in a down clue says this piece sits above the eagle
endless means both outer letters of the word pluck are dropped

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: An eagle with endless pluck flying over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips both ends from PLUCK, leaving LUC; in a down clue 'going over' places it above ERNE. 'pluck' looks like courage but is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: a large Swiss lake, also called the Vierwaldstättersee, around the city of the same name.

clue.text: Susan and Antonia shortly meeting American historian

parts.note: Sue is the short form of Susan

indicators.note: shortly says the name Antonia is cut down to its familiar short form, losing letters at both ends

explanation.surface: Two women with shortened names meet an American scholar of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims Antonia to TONI by dropping AN and the final A; Sue is the usual short form of Susan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman writer of the Lives of the Caesars, he chronicled the first emperors as a historian.

clue.text: Blooming old group of people no longer working

parts.note: flowers that are out are blooming
a faction is a group of people within a larger body

explanation.surface: A flourishing former team of people who have retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads like a British mild swear word but means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a machine or player that is broken or sidelined is not functioning.

clue.text: Yank's check jacket, half-length

indicators.note: half-length takes the first half of the letters of the word for jacket

parts.note: a tabard is a short sleeveless tunic or jacket

explanation.surface: An American checks out a jacket that is cut to half length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-length' keeps the first three of TABARD's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the bill at a bar or restaurant, a check, is what you run up or pick up.

clue.text: Society cuts waste

parts.note: lops means cuts off, as branches from a tree

explanation.surface: Society trims away its rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kitchen scraps and liquid refuse fed to pigs are waste.

clue.text: After it, youngster leaves

indicators.note: after says the youngster comes behind the it piece

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: Having done it, the boy goes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the verb 'goes away' but is the noun, green leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw lettuce and other green leaves; an example rather than a strict synonym.

clue.text: Rock climber following one — look — on way up

indicators.note: following says the climber comes after the turned piece
on way up in a down clue says these letters are read upwards

parts.note: I is one
lo is an old word for look
a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A rock climber goes after one more look on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way up' turns I + LO into OLI, since a down answer reads upward when reversed. LO is an archaic word for look.
explanation.definitionFit: A green silicate mineral common in basalt, found as a rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Queen alone, say, continue to perform without hindrance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the performing phrase goes around the hindrance

parts.note: to sing on is to continue performing a song
a let is a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: The monarch, on her own, carries on performing unimpeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. In bridge a lone queen in a suit is an example of the answer, so 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a lone card of its suit in a hand, such as a bare queen, is an example.

clue.text: Old fellow sporting nice tan

indicators.note: sporting in the sense of wearing or showing off, which here invites rearranging the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An elderly man shows off a pleasing suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' signals an anagram of NICE TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means an aged man, a greybeard, as in Shakespeare's Ancient Pistol.

clue.text: Invoice most of island community, producing a large sum of money

parts.note: a bill is an invoice

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped from the island name

parts.note: Iona is a Hebridean island, home of the Iona Community

explanation.surface: A demand for payment from an island community generates a huge amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of IONA, leaving ION. Iona is a small Scottish island with a well-known religious community.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a huge quantity, here of money.

clue.text: Music from the French composer's last work

parts.note: la is the French feminine for the

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the composer's word is taken

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A piece of music taken from a French composer's final work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes the final letter R of composer's.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece or movement played slowly and broadly takes its name from this tempo marking.

clue.text: Got rid of current emergency procedure

parts.note: fired means sacked, got rid of
a rill is a small stream, a flowing current of water

explanation.surface: Dismissing the present plan for handling a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice evacuation rehearses what to do if a building is ablaze, an emergency procedure.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink fellow brings in matures for fund-raising event

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: brings in says the fellow word takes the maturing word inside it

parts.note: a male is a fellow
ages means matures

explanation.surface: A man introduces aged spirits at a charity do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings in' signals containment: the fellow piece holds the matures piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale of donated second-hand goods held to raise money is a classic charity event.

clue.text: Change tone of start of John Peel song?

definitions.meaning: to colour cloth differently, altering its tone or shade
the hunting song opens with the words ... ken John Peel, a dialect form of do you

explanation.surface: Altering the key at the opening of a song about John Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a Cumbrian huntsman celebrated in a traditional English song beginning in dialect for 'do you know'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring fabric alters its shade, and the song's opening dialect word is spelt the same.

clue.text: Eating with gusto, like a couple of drinks

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: a couple of means the drink word appears twice

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Tucking into food heartily, as one does after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' doubles GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to tuck in or set to with relish is to eat heartily.

clue.text: Proceeds to cover favourite books? That's useless

indicators.note: to cover means the proceeds word wraps around the favourite

parts.note: income is the proceeds of work or investment
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Earnings spent covering beloved books: a hopeless waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' signals containment; NT, the New Testament, is a crossword staple for books.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone lacking the skill to do a job is no good at it.

clue.text: Worked out interpretation of eleven decrees

indicators.note: an interpretation is a new reading of something, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A ruler's reading of eleven edicts has been figured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpretation of' signals an anagram of XI + DECREES. 'Worked out' means trained, not solved.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who has trained physically or had a workout has been to the gym.

clue.text: Stab lodger, one holding son and friend

indicators.note: holding means the lodger word keeps the son letter within it

parts.note: a paying guest is a lodger
I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Knife the lodger, one who is harbouring a son and a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stab' looks like a violent verb but is the noun, as in 'have a stab at'. 'holding' puts S inside GUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is an attempt at guessing, a stab in the colloquial sense.

clue.text: Former Pakistani province reportedly cut off

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: reportedly says the province name is heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: Sind, also Sindh, is a province of Pakistan

explanation.surface: A former Pakistani province has been, they say, severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives a sound-alike of SIND, spelt SCIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare formal word meaning to excise or remove completely by cutting.

clue.text: I will not be included in key staff

indicators.note: will not be included in says the letter I is left out of the key word

parts.note: main means key, principal

explanation.surface: Someone declining to be among the key personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is a verb here, to provide workers for.
explanation.definitionFit: To staff a post or a station is to provide people to work it, synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Men tucked into mostly ripe fruit

indicators.note: tucked into says the men letters are placed inside the ripe word
mostly means the last letter of the ripe word is dropped

parts.note: mellow fruit is ripe and soft
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers tucking into fruit that is not quite fully ripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the W, giving MELLO; 'tucked into' signals containment. OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sour dark cherry used in cooking is a variety of fruit.

clue.text: Something fresh: fish in local cafe, with insides removed

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the pub word

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, an inn
sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: with insides removed keeps only the outside letters of cafe

explanation.surface: A fresh dish: fish served at a nearby cafe, gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub. 'with insides removed' keeps the ends of cafe. 'fresh' means cheeky, not newly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean impudent, so cheeky rudeness is something fresh.

clue.text: Socialist abandoned party in the end

parts.note: left means abandoned, gone away from

indicators.note: in the end takes only the final letter of party

explanation.surface: A socialist eventually walked away from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives Y, the last letter of party.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial: a left-winger, someone on the political left, is a socialist.

clue.text: Persian king lacking power in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: lacking means the island name goes without the power letter

parts.note: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A Persian ruler without authority on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from CYPRUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Founder of the Achaemenid empire, called the Great, he ruled Persia in the sixth century BC.

clue.text: Cleaned up part of church gone round by pious sort

indicators.note: by in the sense of surrounded by, so the pious letters enclose the church piece

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a pious sort

indicators.note: gone round means the part of church is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: a pew is a bench in a church

explanation.surface: A pious person walked round part of a church after tidying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone round' gives WEP; 'by' is read as surrounded by. ST for saint is the crossword's usual pious sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing a floor with a broom cleans it up, synonym in past tense.

clue.text: Dog unexpectedly tearing off, deprived of drink

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the remaining letters are thrown into a surprising new order
deprived of means the drink is taken out of the word tearing

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A dog suddenly dashes away, having been denied a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' takes TEA from TEARING, leaving RING; 'unexpectedly' rearranges RING + OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed: the wire-haired Brussels terrier type is a small dog of this name.

clue.text: Writer not into books originally

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of each of the words not, into and books

explanation.surface: An author who did not start out keen on books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the point of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of a fountain pen does the actual writing, so it is figuratively a writer.

clue.text: A second-rate remedy, free

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
to solve a problem is to remedy it

explanation.surface: A mediocre cure that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' is the verb, to release from guilt, not 'at no cost'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon or release someone from blame or sin is to set them free.

clue.text: Fool employed by renowned dynasty

indicators.note: employed by means the letters are used within the run of words renowned dynasty

explanation.surface: A jester in the service of a famous ruling family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed by' signals the letters are concealed in renowNED DYnasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's pet name, also a dim-witted person: a crossword-familiar sense for a fool.

clue.text: Vegetable ultimately served with most of fish course, we're told

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the fish

parts.note: bream is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: ultimately means only the final letter of served is used
we're told says the word for course is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a route is a course taken

explanation.surface: A vegetable finally served alongside the bulk of a fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' gives BREA; 'ultimately' gives D; 'we're told' turns ROUTE into its sound-alike ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the prairie turnip of North America, a plant with an edible starchy tuber, is a vegetable.
